chapter.li: LEChapter18 Verse1 When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden into which he entered, and his disciples. VerseEnd Verse2 And Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place, for Jesus ofttimes met there with his disciples. VerseEnd Verse3 Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns, and torches, and weapons. VerseEnd Verse4 Jesus, therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth and said unto them, Whom do you seek? VerseEnd Verse5 They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus says unto them, I am he. (And Judas also, who betrayed him, stood with them. VerseEnd) Verse6 As soon then as he had said unto them, I am he, they went backward and fell to the ground. VerseEnd Verse7 Then he asked them again, Whom do you seek? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth. VerseEnd Verse8 Jesus answered, I have told you that I am he. If therefore you seek me, let these go their way VerseEnd — Verse9 that the saying might be fulfilled which he spoke, Of them whom you gave me have I lost none. VerseEnd Verse10 Then Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and smote the high priest’s servant and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus. VerseEnd Verse11 Then said Jesus unto Peter, Put up your sword into the sheath. The cup which my Father has given me, shall I not drink it? VerseEnd

Verse12 Then the band, and the captain, and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him, VerseEnd Verse13 and led him away to Annas first — for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was the high priest that same year. VerseEnd Verse14 Now Caiaphas was he who gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people. VerseEnd

Verse15 And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple — that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest, VerseEnd Verse16 but Peter stood at the door outside. Then went out that other disciple who was known unto the high priest, and spoke unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter. VerseEnd Verse17 Then says the young woman that kept the door unto Peter, Are you not also one of this man’s disciples? He says, I am not. VerseEnd Verse18 And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals (for it was cold and they warmed themselves), and Peter stood with them and warmed himself. VerseEnd

Verse19 The high priest then asked Jesus of his disciples and of his doctrine. VerseEnd Verse20 Jesus answered him, I spoke openly to the world. I ever taught in the synagogue and in the temple where the Jews always assemble, and in secret have I said nothing. VerseEnd Verse21 Why do you ask me? Ask them who heard me what I have said unto them. Behold, they know what I said. VerseEnd Verse22 And when he had thus spoken, one of the officers who stood by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Do you answer the high priest so? VerseEnd Verse23 Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil, but if well, why do you smite me? VerseEnd Verse24 Now Annas sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest. VerseEnd

Verse25 And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Are you not also one of his disciples? He denied it and said, I am not. VerseEnd Verse26 One of the servants of the high priest, being his kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, says, Did I not see you in the garden with him? VerseEnd Verse27 Peter then denied again and immediately the cock crowed. VerseEnd

Verse28 Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas unto the hall of judgment, and it was early. And they themselves went not into the judgment hall, lest they should be defiled, but that they might eat the passover. VerseEnd Verse29 Pilate then went out unto them and said, What accusation do you bring against this man? VerseEnd Verse30 They answered and said unto him, If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up unto you. VerseEnd Verse31 Then said Pilate unto them, Take him and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death VerseEnd — Verse32 that the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke signifying what death he should die. VerseEnd

Verse33 Then Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus and said unto him, Are you the king of the Jews? VerseEnd Verse34 Jesus answered him, Do you say this thing of yourself? Or did others tell it to you of me? VerseEnd Verse35 Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests have delivered you unto me. What have you done? VerseEnd Verse36 Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews. But now is my kingdom not from here. VerseEnd Verse37 Pilate therefore said unto him, Are you a king then? Jesus answered, You say that I am a king; to this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world — that I should bear witness unto the truth. Everyone that is of the truth hears my voice. VerseEnd Verse38 Pilate says unto him, What is truth?

And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and says unto them, I find in him no fault at all; VerseEnd Verse39 but you have a custom that I should release unto you one at the Passover. Do you desire therefore that I release unto you the king of the Jews? VerseEnd Verse40 Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas! (Now Barabbas was a robber. VerseEnd) LEChapter19 Verse1 Then Pilate therefore took Jesus and scourged him. VerseEnd Verse2 And the soldiers plaited a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe VerseEnd Verse3 and said, Hail, king of the Jews! And they smote him with their hands. VerseEnd

Verse4 Pilate therefore went forth again, and says unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you that you may know that I find no fault in him. VerseEnd Verse5 Then came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. And Pilate says unto them, Behold the man! VerseEnd Verse6 When the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him! Pilate says unto them, Take him and crucify him, for I find no fault in him. VerseEnd Verse7 The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die because he made himself the Son of God. VerseEnd

Verse8 When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he was the more afraid, VerseEnd Verse9 and went again into the judgment hall, and says unto Jesus, Where are you from? But Jesus gave him no answer. VerseEnd Verse10 Then says Pilate unto him, You do not speak unto me? Do you not know that I have power to crucify you? And have power to release you? VerseEnd Verse11 Jesus answered, You could have no power at all against me except it were given you from above. Therefore, he that delivered me unto you has the greater sin. VerseEnd Verse12 And from that time forth, Pilate sought to release him.

But the Jews cried out, saying, If you let this man go, you are not Caesar’s friend! Whoever makes himself a king speaks against Caesar! VerseEnd Verse13 When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement (but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha) VerseEnd. Verse14 And it was the preparation of the Passover and about the sixth hour, and he says unto the Jews, Behold your king! VerseEnd Verse15 But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him! Pilate says unto them, Shall I crucify your king? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar. VerseEnd Verse16 Then he delivered him therefore unto them to be crucified.

And they took Jesus and led him away. VerseEnd Verse17 And he, bearing his cross, went forth into a place called the place of a burial (which is called in the Hebrew, Golgotha) VerseEnd Verse18 where they crucified him and two others with him — on either side one, and Jesus in the middle. VerseEnd Verse19 And Pilate wrote a title and put it on the cross, and the writing was: jesus of nazareth the king of the jews VerseEnd. Verse20 This title then read many of the Jews, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near to the city, and it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin. VerseEnd Verse21 Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not: the king of the jews, but that: He said, I am king of the Jews. VerseEnd Verse22 Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written. VerseEnd Verse23 Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part, and also his coat. Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout. VerseEnd Verse24 They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be — that the scripture might be fulfilled which says: They parted my raiment among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did. VerseEnd

Verse25 Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleopas, and Mary Magdalene. VerseEnd Verse26 When Jesus therefore saw his mother and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he says unto his mother, Woman, behold your son. VerseEnd Verse27 Then says he to the disciple, Behold your mother. And from that hour, that disciple took her unto his own home. VerseEnd

Verse28 After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, says, I thirst. VerseEnd Verse29 Now there was a vessel full of vinegar mingled with gall, and they filled a sponge with it and put upon hyssop, and put to his mouth. VerseEnd Verse30 When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished. And he bowed his head and gave up the ghost. VerseEnd

Verse31 The Jews, therefore, because it was the preparation — that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the Sabbath day (for that Sabbath day was a high day) — implored Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away. VerseEnd Verse32 Then came the soldiers and broke the legs of the first and of the other who was crucified with him. VerseEnd Verse33 But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was dead already, they broke not his legs, VerseEnd Verse34 but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side and immediately came there out blood and water. VerseEnd Verse35 And he that saw it bore record and his record is true. And he knows that he speaks truth, that you might believe. VerseEnd Verse36 For these things were done that the scripture should be fulfilled: A bone of him shall not be broken. VerseEnd Verse37 And again another scripture says: They shall look on him whom they pierced. VerseEnd

Verse38 And after this, Joseph of Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus (but secretly, for fear of the Jews), implored Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus, and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore and took the body of Jesus. VerseEnd Verse39 And there came also Nicodemus, who at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pound weight. VerseEnd Verse40 Then took they the body of Jesus and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury. VerseEnd Verse41 Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new sepulcher wherein was never man yet laid. VerseEnd Verse42 There they laid Jesus therefore because of the Jews’ preparation day, for the sepulcher was near at hand. VerseEnd
